programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Às dèidh toiseach tòiseachaidh dùbhlanach, lean Somhairle agus Innes orra a’ rothaireachd air a Bhadger Divide, far an tàinig iad tarsainn air duilgheadasan meacanaigeach; uisge trom; geàrr-rathaidean; tionndadh ceàrr agus bagannan caillte! Thàinig an rothaiche agus an neach-gleidhidh chlàran, Kerry Nic a’Phì, còmhla riutha airson earrann. After a tough start, Somhairle and Innes continue riding the Badger Divide, where they encounter mechanical issues, torrential rain, shortcuts, wrong turns and lost baggage! They’re joined for a section by record-holder, cyclist Kerry MacPhee.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Tha Somhairle agus Niamh a’deanamh rud beag ‘pacadh-baidhsagal’, a’ cuir seachad trì laithichean ‘socair sàmhach’ a’ rothaireachd air Slighe Thaobh Spè. Somhairle introduces Niamh to ‘bikepacking’, opting for a ‘relaxed’ three-days cycling the Speyside Way.

programme.title: Abigail

programme.desc: Spòrs beò agus geàrr-chunntasan an latha bho Glaschu 2026. Air a lìbhrigeadh le Derek ‘Pluto’ Moireach agus sgioba aithris BBC ALBA. Live sporting action and highlights from Glasgow 2026. Presented by Derek ‘Pluto’ Murray and BBC ALBA’s commentary team.

programme.title: Eòrpa
programme.desc: Aithris bho 2016 le Angela NicIlleathain, le agallamhan le daoine a chur seachad bliadhnaichean ann am prìosan ainmeil nan Stàitean Aonaichte ann am Bàgh Ghuantanamo fo amharras ceannairc. Angela Maclean’s award-winning 2016 report, featuring exclusive interviews with former detainees at the notorious US prison at Guantanamo Bay.

programme.title: Cuirm aig Celtic
programme.desc: Cuirm-chiùil à Talla Rìoghail Ghlaschu le Capercaillie agus Orcastra a’ BhBC ann an Alba. Capercaillie and The BBC SSO collaborate in a performance at Glasgow Royal Concert Hall.

programme.title: Rudan Beaga Bòidheach/Life’s Little Things
programme.desc: Tha Niamh NicFhionghain a’ coinneachadh daoine òga eile gus rudan beaga fheuchainn a tha a’ toirt toileachas dhaibh. Bho Iòga air mullach cnoc, a bhith a’ sgrìobhadh bàrdachd, gu furachas, dòigh-beatha a’ bhana-campachaidh no a bhith a’ cluich camanachd – tha tòrr ann air an urrainn dhut a bhith taingeil an uair a tha thu air a’ bhlàr a-muigh. Skye digital creator Niamh Mackinnon meets other young people to try out the different little activities that spark joy for them. From hilltop yoga, writing poems, mindfulness, campervan life to playing shinty - there’s so much to appreciate when you just get out there. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Na Sgiobairean mu Dheireadh/The Last Captains
programme.desc: Tha seusan a’ ghiomaich a’ tòiseachadh le brag air na h-eileanan – gun chuòta, gun tròcair. Tha gach soitheach na dhian-ruith gus an tuarastal a tha deatamach a chosnadh. Lobster season explodes on the Maggies - no quotas, no mercy. It’s a rat race on the water, with every trap chasing a make-or-break payday. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: Some 350 million years ago, evolution reached one of its most crucial stages when fish crawled from the water onto the land and became amphibians. Today, newts, salamanders, toads and frogs still survive in great quantities, and there is even one species of frog where the male gives birth from its mouth! Presented by David Attenborough.

programme.title: Voyages of Discovery
programme.desc: Explorer Paul Rose tells the story of three Frenchmen who couldn't stand each other, yet set off on an eight-year scientific mission in one of the most hostile places on the planet. Their plan, to settle an international row by measuring the shape of the planet, took them to the disease-ridden rainforests and oxygen-starved peaks of the Ecuadorian Andes. Rose follows in the footsteps of the 18th-century explorers who were complete innocents abroad and had no idea of the horrors they were letting themselves in for. Despite disease, death and some highly disastrous sexual liaisons, the men made discoveries that fundamentally changed all our lives.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: Paul Atterbury embarks on an alluring journey into the golden age of ocean liners, finding out how these great ships made such a mark on the popular imagination and why they continue to enchant to this day. Paul's voyage takes him around Britain and reveals a story of design, politics, propaganda, Hollywood glamour and tragedy. Along the way, he uncovers some amazing survivals from the liners of the past - a cinema in Scotland built from the interiors of the SS Homeric, a house in Poole in which cabins from the Mauretania are lovingly preserved - as well as the design inspiration behind the first great liners.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: The Sinfonia of London transcend in a programme brimming with colourful orchestration under the baton of their ever-popular artistic director, John Wilson. Opening with Verdi’s thunderous overture to La Forza del Destino, followed by Norwegian cellist Jonathan Aasgaard in his Proms soloist debut with Walton’s hypnotic Cello Concerto and finishing with the music time capsule that is Respighi’s enchanting sun-drenched Roman Trilogy. Presented by Katie Derham from the Royal Albert Hall.

programme.title: China's Greatest Treasures
programme.desc: The Yellow River - running for almost five and half thousand kilometres from west to east - is known as China's mother river. It's hailed as the cradle of Chinese civilisation and over thousands of years, it has fed billions of people and inspired generations of artists. Alastair explores the Yellow River and discovers some of the finest artwork from its valley, to understand how this unique natural phenomenon is deeply connected with the identity of the Chinese and the roots of their culture.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI Decoded explores the growing backlash against artificial intelligence. As fears of job losses spread through the tech industry and protests against AI data centres gather momentum, we ask whether the promises of an AI-powered future are starting to unravel. Plus, could advanced AI one day become conscious, and if it does, what responsibilities would we have towards it? Presenter Marc Cieslak is joined by digital rights activist Cory Doctorow, AI entrepreneur Priya Lakhani and academic Dr Ella Hafermalz to unpack the biggest questions facing AI today.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: An AI-generated actor called Tilly Norwood has been cast in the lead role of a forthcoming film, adding to the debate about artificial intelligence in filmmaking. The announcement follows criticism from actors such as Emily Blunt, and objections from the US performers' union. Eline Van der Velden, founder and CEO of Particle6, explains why she created Tilly Norwood, while Jake Kanter, international investigations editor at Deadline, sets out the reaction from the film industry. Andy Burnham has become the UK's new prime minister, and his approach to the media is already attracting attention. His team has relied more on social media, online creators and direct communication than on traditional broadcast interviews. Lizzy Buchan, political editor of the Daily Mirror; Jennifer Gerber, senior political advisor, WA Communications; Tom Nicholas, creator of the Slow News Day YouTube channel; and broadcaster Andrew Neil, presenter of The Andrew Neil Report, assess what this could mean for political journalism and public accountability.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: An AI-generated actor called Tilly Norwood has been cast in the lead role of a forthcoming film, adding to the debate about artificial intelligence in filmmaking. The announcement follows criticism from actors such as Emily Blunt, and objections from the US performers' union. Eline Van der Velden, founder and CEO of Particle6, explains why she created Tilly Norwood, while Jake Kanter, international investigations editor at Deadline, sets out the reaction from the film industry. Andy Burnham has become the UK's new prime minister, and his approach to the media is already attracting attention. His team has relied more on social media, online creators and direct communication than on traditional broadcast interviews. Lizzy Buchan, political editor of the Daily Mirror; Jennifer Gerber, senior political advisor, WA Communications; Tom Nicholas, creator of the Slow News Day YouTube channel; and broadcaster Andrew Neil, presenter of The Andrew Neil Report, assess what this could mean for political journalism and public accountability.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. This week, in the aftermath of a political earthquake in Hungary, Stephanie Hegarty explores whether the downfall of Viktor Orbán could be a warning sign for populist leaders everywhere, and BBC Eye investigates the Russian nationalists who are taking the law into their own hands.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Alistair Appleton faces his toughest assignment to date as he attempts to find broadcasting icon and one of TV’s most opinionated panellists, Janet Street-Porter, a Suffolk sanctuary - away from the many daily irritations she’d happily banish from existence. Despite Janet’s refreshingly short and sweet wish list, it proves to be a tricky challenge satisfying this exacting house hunter. However, Alistair has an ace up his sleeve, which sees the property search take an epic detour to a remote Hebridean island.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Sefton Park in Liverpool, where Chinese ceramics expert Lars Tharp sees a rare double Ming dynasty vase bought in a charity shop, Raj Bisram discovers some valuable Beatles memorabilia, and Dendy Easton admires a painting by George Melly. Expert Ronnie Archer-Morgan is almost tricked by an intriguing Grand Tour bronze, Andy McConnell falls in love with some unusual Finnish glass, and Raj is excited to see a silver disc brought in by one of the members of Gerry and the Pacemakers. Will Farmer challenges Fiona Bruce to guess the values of three vases by pioneering female artists, and Fiona discovers the history behind the famous Palm House in Sefton Park.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Child psychologist Dr Gabrielle 'Gabs' Fox is recovering from the trauma of a car accident that killed her husband, Alex, and left her paralysed. Grieving and guilt-ridden, she has moved to the coastal town of Porth Hen in South Wales and is slowly learning to rebuild her life with the help of her own psychologist, Mel. Gabs accepts a position at Oxsmith Psychiatric Hospital, where she is assigned several new patients, including the unit’s most disturbed patient, 17-year-old Bethany Krall. Dangerous, intelligent and manipulative, Bethany was sectioned two years ago for the brutal murder of her mother, Carys Krall. The crime shocked the nation, not least because Bethany’s bereft father, Leonard Krall, is the charismatic leader of the Faith Way, a feelgood religious movement boasting millions of followers thanks to its reassuring motto 'Choose Hope'. But when Gabs reads Bethany’s case file, she finds the previous psychologist left very few notes.

Grieving and guilt-ridden, she has moved to the coastal town of Porth Hen in South Wales and is slowly learning to rebuild her life with the help of her own psychologist, Mel. Gabs accepts a position at Oxsmith Psychiatric Hospital, where she is assigned several new patients, including the unit’s most disturbed patient, 17-year-old Bethany Krall. Dangerous, intelligent and manipulative, Bethany was sectioned two years ago for the brutal murder of her mother, Carys Krall. The crime shocked the nation, not least because Bethany’s bereft father, Leonard Krall, is the charismatic leader of the Faith Way, a feelgood religious movement boasting millions of followers thanks to its reassuring motto 'Choose Hope'. But when Gabs reads Bethany’s case file, she finds the previous psychologist left very few notes.

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection
programme.desc: Nottingham Liberal Synagogue, part of the Progressive Judaism movement, guide us into the Sabbath with their musical Friday evening service, known as Erev Shabbat. Led by Rabbi Gili Zidkiyahu alongside co-Rabbi Josh Levy, this inclusive musical service welcomes all members of the community together to usher in the Sabbath. With liturgical guidance from our prayer leaders, the service blends ancient psalms and prayers, including the Sh’ma (prayer and declaration of faith) and a silent Amidah (offering time for personal reflection) with poetry and hymns. After the blessing of the challah, a traditional Jewish bread, and the Kiddush (sanctification of the wine), the community enjoy a light bring-and-share supper in the synagogue and talk about what being part of the Progressive Judaism movement means to them.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: Seven celebrities of differing faiths and beliefs experience an emotional journey on a pilgrimage in north Wales, a route linked by churches dedicated to early Celtic Christian saints. Immersing themselves on this spiritual journey are wildlife presenter Michaela Strachan, who places her faith in the natural world; Spencer Matthews, a former Made in Chelsea reality star who was christened in the Church of England but is still searching for answers to life’s big questions; Sonali Shah, a journalist and TV presenter who grew up in a Jain family; comedian Eshaan Akbar, a lapsed Muslim; Amanda Lovett, a practising Catholic who was catapulted into the public eye in the first series of Traitors; actor Tom Rosenthal of Friday Night Dinner fame, who is areligious; and TV personality and former model Christine McGuinness, who is spiritual but doesn’t practise one particular faith. Travelling on foot and by bus, the seven pilgrims begin their adventure at Flint Castle on the bank of the Dee Estuary and follow the coastal path to Greenfield Valley, the official start of the 220km Pilgrim’s Way.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Sefton Park in Liverpool, where Chinese ceramics expert Lars Tharp sees a rare double Ming dynasty vase bought in a charity shop, Raj Bisram discovers some valuable Beatles memorabilia, and Dendy Easton admires a painting by George Melly. Expert Ronnie Archer-Morgan is almost tricked by an intriguing Grand Tour bronze, Andy McConnell falls in love with some unusual Finnish glass, and Raj is excited to see a silver disc brought in by one of the members of Gerry and the Pacemakers. Will Farmer challenges Fiona Bruce to guess the values of three vases by pioneering female artists, and Fiona discovers the history behind the famous Palm House in Sefton Park.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

Expert Ronnie Archer-Morgan is almost tricked by an intriguing Grand Tour bronze, Andy McConnell falls in love with some unusual Finnish glass, and Raj is excited to see a silver disc brought in by one of the members of Gerry and the Pacemakers. Will Farmer challenges Fiona Bruce to guess the values of three vases by pioneering female artists, and Fiona discovers the history behind the famous Palm House in Sefton Park.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Child psychologist Dr Gabrielle 'Gabs' Fox is recovering from the trauma of a car accident that killed her husband, Alex, and left her paralysed. Grieving and guilt-ridden, she has moved to the coastal town of Porth Hen in South Wales and is slowly learning to rebuild her life with the help of her own psychologist, Mel. Gabs accepts a position at Oxsmith Psychiatric Hospital, where she is assigned several new patients, including the unit’s most disturbed patient, 17-year-old Bethany Krall. Dangerous, intelligent and manipulative, Bethany was sectioned two years ago for the brutal murder of her mother, Carys Krall. The crime shocked the nation, not least because Bethany’s bereft father, Leonard Krall, is the charismatic leader of the Faith Way, a feelgood religious movement boasting millions of followers thanks to its reassuring motto 'Choose Hope'. But when Gabs reads Bethany’s case file, she finds the previous psychologist left very few notes.

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Alistair Appleton faces his toughest assignment to date as he attempts to find broadcasting icon and one of TV’s most opinionated panellists, Janet Street-Porter, a Suffolk sanctuary - away from the many daily irritations she’d happily banish from existence. programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Sefton Park in Liverpool, where Chinese ceramics expert Lars Tharp sees a rare double Ming dynasty vase bought in a charity shop, Raj Bisram discovers some valuable Beatles memorabilia, and Dendy Easton admires a painting by George Melly. Expert Ronnie Archer-Morgan is almost tricked by an intriguing Grand Tour bronze, Andy McConnell falls in love with some unusual Finnish glass, and Raj is excited to see a silver disc brought in by one of the members of Gerry and the Pacemakers. Will Farmer challenges Fiona Bruce to guess the values of three vases by pioneering female artists, and Fiona discovers the history behind the famous Palm House in Sefton Park.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Child psychologist Dr Gabrielle 'Gabs' Fox is recovering from the trauma of a car accident that killed her husband, Alex, and left her paralysed. Grieving and guilt-ridden, she has moved to the coastal town of Porth Hen in South Wales and is slowly learning to rebuild her life with the help of her own psychologist, Mel. Gabs accepts a position at Oxsmith Psychiatric Hospital, where she is assigned several new patients, including the unit’s most disturbed patient, 17-year-old Bethany Krall. Dangerous, intelligent and manipulative, Bethany was sectioned two years ago for the brutal murder of her mother, Carys Krall. The crime shocked the nation, not least because Bethany’s bereft father, Leonard Krall, is the charismatic leader of the Faith Way, a feelgood religious movement boasting millions of followers thanks to its reassuring motto 'Choose Hope'. But when Gabs reads Bethany’s case file, she finds the previous psychologist left very few notes.

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection
programme.desc: Nottingham Liberal Synagogue, part of the Progressive Judaism movement, guide us into the Sabbath with their musical Friday evening service, known as Erev Shabbat. Led by Rabbi Gili Zidkiyahu alongside co-Rabbi Josh Levy, this inclusive musical service welcomes all members of the community together to usher in the Sabbath. With liturgical guidance from our prayer leaders, the service blends ancient psalms and prayers, including the Sh’ma (prayer and declaration of faith) and a silent Amidah (offering time for personal reflection) with poetry and hymns. After the blessing of the challah, a traditional Jewish bread, and the Kiddush (sanctification of the wine), the community enjoy a light bring-and-share supper in the synagogue and talk about what being part of the Progressive Judaism movement means to them.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: Seven celebrities of differing faiths and beliefs experience an emotional journey on a pilgrimage in north Wales, a route linked by churches dedicated to early Celtic Christian saints. Immersing themselves on this spiritual journey are wildlife presenter Michaela Strachan, who places her faith in the natural world; Spencer Matthews, a former Made in Chelsea reality star who was christened in the Church of England but is still searching for answers to life’s big questions; Sonali Shah, a journalist and TV presenter who grew up in a Jain family; comedian Eshaan Akbar, a lapsed Muslim; Amanda Lovett, a practising Catholic who was catapulted into the public eye in the first series of Traitors; actor Tom Rosenthal of Friday Night Dinner fame, who is areligious; and TV personality and former model Christine McGuinness, who is spiritual but doesn’t practise one particular faith. Travelling on foot and by bus, the seven pilgrims begin their adventure at Flint Castle on the bank of the Dee Estuary and follow the coastal path to Greenfield Valley, the official start of the 220km Pilgrim’s Way.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Buckinghamshire, Sarah Moore scours Beaconsfield recycling centre for items that can be given a new lease of life rather than hitting the skips. programme.title: Wales' Home of the Year
programme.desc: It’s the Grand Final! Judges Owain Wyn Evans, interior designer Mandy Watkins, and architectural designer Glen Thomas have scoured the country in search of Wales’ home of the year 2026. It’s now down to the final five homes – the winners of each regional episode – to go head-to-head. But only one of them can be the winner of the prestigious title. The judges have invited the five regional winners to join them at the grand Victorian Gothic mansion, Insole Court, in Cardiff. Here the judges will go through the homes one by one scoring them on architectural merit, distinctive design and original style, before whittling five down to three, and then – the hardest job of all – choosing the overall winner of Wales’ Home of the Year 2026.

It’s now down to the final five homes – the winners of each regional episode – to go head-to-head. But only one of them can be the winner of the prestigious title. The judges have invited the five regional winners to join them at the grand Victorian Gothic mansion, Insole Court, in Cardiff. Here the judges will go through the homes one by one scoring them on architectural merit, distinctive design and original style, before whittling five down to three, and then – the hardest job of all – choosing the overall winner of Wales’ Home of the Year 2026.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: An intimate portrait of Northern Irish dancer Melissa Hamilton, charting her late start, fierce determination and rise to principal with the Royal Ballet against all expectations.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Sefton Park in Liverpool, where Chinese ceramics expert Lars Tharp sees a rare double Ming dynasty vase bought in a charity shop, Raj Bisram discovers some valuable Beatles memorabilia, and Dendy Easton admires a painting by George Melly. Expert Ronnie Archer-Morgan is almost tricked by an intriguing Grand Tour bronze, Andy McConnell falls in love with some unusual Finnish glass, and Raj is excited to see a silver disc brought in by one of the members of Gerry and the Pacemakers. Will Farmer challenges Fiona Bruce to guess the values of three vases by pioneering female artists, and Fiona discovers the history behind the famous Palm House in Sefton Park.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Child psychologist Dr Gabrielle 'Gabs' Fox is recovering from the trauma of a car accident that killed her husband, Alex, and left her paralysed. Grieving and guilt-ridden, she has moved to the coastal town of Porth Hen in South Wales and is slowly learning to rebuild her life with the help of her own psychologist, Mel. Gabs accepts a position at Oxsmith Psychiatric Hospital, where she is assigned several new patients, including the unit’s most disturbed patient, 17-year-old Bethany Krall. Dangerous, intelligent and manipulative, Bethany was sectioned two years ago for the brutal murder of her mother, Carys Krall. The crime shocked the nation, not least because Bethany’s bereft father, Leonard Krall, is the charismatic leader of the Faith Way, a feelgood religious movement boasting millions of followers thanks to its reassuring motto 'Choose Hope'. But when Gabs reads Bethany’s case file, she finds the previous psychologist left very few notes.

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection
programme.desc: Nottingham Liberal Synagogue, part of the Progressive Judaism movement, guide us into the Sabbath with their musical Friday evening service, known as Erev Shabbat. Led by Rabbi Gili Zidkiyahu alongside co-Rabbi Josh Levy, this inclusive musical service welcomes all members of the community together to usher in the Sabbath. With liturgical guidance from our prayer leaders, the service blends ancient psalms and prayers, including the Sh’ma (prayer and declaration of faith) and a silent Amidah (offering time for personal reflection) with poetry and hymns. After the blessing of the challah, a traditional Jewish bread, and the Kiddush (sanctification of the wine), the community enjoy a light bring-and-share supper in the synagogue and talk about what being part of the Progressive Judaism movement means to them.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: Seven celebrities of differing faiths and beliefs experience an emotional journey on a pilgrimage in north Wales, a route linked by churches dedicated to early Celtic Christian saints. Immersing themselves on this spiritual journey are wildlife presenter Michaela Strachan, who places her faith in the natural world; Spencer Matthews, a former Made in Chelsea reality star who was christened in the Church of England but is still searching for answers to life’s big questions; Sonali Shah, a journalist and TV presenter who grew up in a Jain family; comedian Eshaan Akbar, a lapsed Muslim; Amanda Lovett, a practising Catholic who was catapulted into the public eye in the first series of Traitors; actor Tom Rosenthal of Friday Night Dinner fame, who is areligious; and TV personality and former model Christine McGuinness, who is spiritual but doesn’t practise one particular faith. Travelling on foot and by bus, the seven pilgrims begin their adventure at Flint Castle on the bank of the Dee Estuary and follow the coastal path to Greenfield Valley, the official start of the 220km Pilgrim’s Way.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Buckinghamshire, Sarah Moore scours Beaconsfield recycling centre for items that can be given a new lease of life rather than hitting the skips. A retro orange armchair is a task for upholsterer Leanne Watts, while upcycling siblings Katie Stone and Sophie Lawrence want to add a 60s groove to a tallboy and dresser set. For her own project, Sarah has a vision for some discarded spectacle cases, but will they see a profit when she comes to sell?

programme.desc: Alistair Appleton faces his toughest assignment to date as he attempts to find broadcasting icon and one of TV’s most opinionated panellists, Janet Street-Porter, a Suffolk sanctuary - away from the many daily irritations she’d happily banish from existence. Despite Janet’s refreshingly short and sweet wish list, it proves to be a tricky challenge satisfying this exacting house hunter. However, Alistair has an ace up his sleeve, which sees the property search take an epic detour to a remote Hebridean island.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Sefton Park in Liverpool, where Chinese ceramics expert Lars Tharp sees a rare double Ming dynasty vase bought in a charity shop, Raj Bisram discovers some valuable Beatles memorabilia, and Dendy Easton admires a painting by George Melly. Expert Ronnie Archer-Morgan is almost tricked by an intriguing Grand Tour bronze, Andy McConnell falls in love with some unusual Finnish glass, and Raj is excited to see a silver disc brought in by one of the members of Gerry and the Pacemakers. Will Farmer challenges Fiona Bruce to guess the values of three vases by pioneering female artists, and Fiona discovers the history behind the famous Palm House in Sefton Park.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Child psychologist Dr Gabrielle 'Gabs' Fox is recovering from the trauma of a car accident that killed her husband, Alex, and left her paralysed. Grieving and guilt-ridden, she has moved to the coastal town of Porth Hen in South Wales and is slowly learning to rebuild her life with the help of her own psychologist, Mel. Gabs accepts a position at Oxsmith Psychiatric Hospital, where she is assigned several new patients, including the unit’s most disturbed patient, 17-year-old Bethany Krall. Dangerous, intelligent and manipulative, Bethany was sectioned two years ago for the brutal murder of her mother, Carys Krall. The crime shocked the nation, not least because Bethany’s bereft father, Leonard Krall, is the charismatic leader of the Faith Way, a feelgood religious movement boasting millions of followers thanks to its reassuring motto 'Choose Hope'. But when Gabs reads Bethany’s case file, she finds the previous psychologist left very few notes.

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection
programme.desc: Nottingham Liberal Synagogue, part of the Progressive Judaism movement, guide us into the Sabbath with their musical Friday evening service, known as Erev Shabbat. Led by Rabbi Gili Zidkiyahu alongside co-Rabbi Josh Levy, this inclusive musical service welcomes all members of the community together to usher in the Sabbath. With liturgical guidance from our prayer leaders, the service blends ancient psalms and prayers, including the Sh’ma (prayer and declaration of faith) and a silent Amidah (offering time for personal reflection) with poetry and hymns. After the blessing of the challah, a traditional Jewish bread, and the Kiddush (sanctification of the wine), the community enjoy a light bring-and-share supper in the synagogue and talk about what being part of the Progressive Judaism movement means to them.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: Seven celebrities of differing faiths and beliefs experience an emotional journey on a pilgrimage in north Wales, a route linked by churches dedicated to early Celtic Christian saints. Immersing themselves on this spiritual journey are wildlife presenter Michaela Strachan, who places her faith in the natural world; Spencer Matthews, a former Made in Chelsea reality star who was christened in the Church of England but is still searching for answers to life’s big questions; Sonali Shah, a journalist and TV presenter who grew up in a Jain family; comedian Eshaan Akbar, a lapsed Muslim; Amanda Lovett, a practising Catholic who was catapulted into the public eye in the first series of Traitors; actor Tom Rosenthal of Friday Night Dinner fame, who is areligious; and TV personality and former model Christine McGuinness, who is spiritual but doesn’t practise one particular faith. Travelling on foot and by bus, the seven pilgrims begin their adventure at Flint Castle on the bank of the Dee Estuary and follow the coastal path to Greenfield Valley, the official start of the 220km Pilgrim’s Way.

programme.desc: Alistair Appleton faces his toughest assignment to date as he attempts to find broadcasting icon and one of TV’s most opinionated panellists, Janet Street-Porter, a Suffolk sanctuary - away from the many daily irritations she’d happily banish from existence. Despite Janet’s refreshingly short and sweet wish list, it proves to be a tricky challenge satisfying this exacting house hunter. However, Alistair has an ace up his sleeve, which sees the property search take an epic detour to a remote Hebridean island.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Sefton Park in Liverpool, where Chinese ceramics expert Lars Tharp sees a rare double Ming dynasty vase bought in a charity shop, Raj Bisram discovers some valuable Beatles memorabilia, and Dendy Easton admires a painting by George Melly. Expert Ronnie Archer-Morgan is almost tricked by an intriguing Grand Tour bronze, Andy McConnell falls in love with some unusual Finnish glass, and Raj is excited to see a silver disc brought in by one of the members of Gerry and the Pacemakers. Will Farmer challenges Fiona Bruce to guess the values of three vases by pioneering female artists, and Fiona discovers the history behind the famous Palm House in Sefton Park.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Child psychologist Dr Gabrielle 'Gabs' Fox is recovering from the trauma of a car accident that killed her husband, Alex, and left her paralysed. Grieving and guilt-ridden, she has moved to the coastal town of Porth Hen in South Wales and is slowly learning to rebuild her life with the help of her own psychologist, Mel. Gabs accepts a position at Oxsmith Psychiatric Hospital, where she is assigned several new patients, including the unit’s most disturbed patient, 17-year-old Bethany Krall. Dangerous, intelligent and manipulative, Bethany was sectioned two years ago for the brutal murder of her mother, Carys Krall. The crime shocked the nation, not least because Bethany’s bereft father, Leonard Krall, is the charismatic leader of the Faith Way, a feelgood religious movement boasting millions of followers thanks to its reassuring motto 'Choose Hope'. But when Gabs reads Bethany’s case file, she finds the previous psychologist left very few notes.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Dom and Lucia help an iconic Glasgow landmark that has lost its lustre, save an endangered Chinese unicorn, and discover how street art is changing one city before our very eyes.

programme.title: Island Crossings
programme.desc: A freight backlog in Stornoway has area operations manager Fiona struggling to keep supply lines to the isles open, and CalMac trainee sisters Tanya and Natalie go to sea.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: In Glasgow, Paul and Ryan of the Special Operations Response Team are called to a siege in a flat where a man has barricaded himself inside and is threatening to harm himself. It’s a difficult and emotional situation, and the team must coordinate with the police at the scene to try to ensure the best outcome. Meanwhile, Aberdeen-based teammates Kirsty and Bruce are called to see Rebecca, who has suffered an anaphylactic attack. The crew administer several doses of adrenaline, but Rebecca shows little signs of improvement, prompting a rapid journey on blue lights to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. From the lowlands to the Highlands, the Scottish Air Ambulance Service delivers help to every part of the country. Serving as a paramedic on the King Air fixed-wing aircraft, Stephen travels to the Isle of Lewis. William is visiting the islands as part of a golfing holiday but has fractured his ribs in a fall, necessitating a transfer to the mainland.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Sitcom featuring Jack and Victor, two irrepressible pensioners first seen in the comedy series Chewin' the Fat, along with their dependable pals Winston and Tam, fresh out of Craiglang and taking on the world. Jack and Victor are worried that old Bert has gone downhill since his wife died. Meanwhile Winston has acquired a limp and a home help. Could romance be on the cards?

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Bams beware - the force is back on duty - and this bunch have got Scotland's back. It's all kicking off in the new series of the hit spoof documentary. The cops get an unwanted eyeful, a surprising faceful and a stupefying skinful. This episode introduces some new recruits - Megan Squire and Andrea McGill - plain-talking plain-clothes detectives - cops fully cognisant of the word on the street. Meanwhile, the series starts with a bang when Bobby fidgets with something explosive that officer Karen told him to keep his paws off.

programme.title: Ooh the Banter
programme.desc: Jack Docherty brings together a jam-packed cast of comedians, actors and famous faces for a riotous celebration of Scotland's most valuable export – its sense of humour. Scotland is a small nation with a big funny bone. It's known the world over for self-deprecation, quick-witted patter and deadpan asides. But what makes it so funny? To find out the answer, this programme delves deep into the BBC Scotland archives to find a century’s worth of classic characters, catchphrases and comedy clips. A line is drawn from the early days of Scottish comedy on TV from the McFlannels, Stanley Baxter and Lex McLean through to the modern generation of quickfire online sensations. The medium may have changed, but the essence of the humour remains the same - colourful language, authenticity, irreverence and flair for creative insults. Joining Jack will be some of Scotland’s most iconic comedy talent such as Elaine C Smith, Alex Norton, Karen Dunbar, Lawrence Chaney, Brian Cox, Alan Cumming and Forbes Masson.

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: It's Aks's prom night, but will Mobeen let her go? With rumours about the debauchery at previous proms and the threat of a stabbing, Mobeen must safeguard her at any cost. Things get complicated when a classmate of Aks's, Ridwan, makes some very unwise decisions that leave Mobeen very concerned. Eight, meanwhile, is in danger of getting in too deep with a local wide boy, and he is potentially going to drag everyone down with him. Can Mobeen manage to keep everyone out of trouble?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: When Aks breaks her shoulder and heads for hospital with the boys, Accident and Emergency is the state of play. With Mobeen, Eight and Nate looking shifty de facto, the authorities start to get suspicious about how Aks may have sustained her injuries. In the waiting room, we see life in an overstretched A&E and the gang in a constant battle to prove their innocence, battle prejudice and, of course, keep Pakistani Rain Man (Eight) out of trouble.

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: They say the past is never far away. And for Mobeen, it’s about to punch him in the throat. Can he stay clear of trouble, or are things about to take a turn for the worse?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: Dogs and ethnic minorities have a very bad track record. So when a clip involving Mobeen and an Alsatian goes viral, it’s a disaster. Aks is drawn in by the prospect of internet fame, while Mobeen tries to see if the spark between him and Aks’s teacher, Miss Aitken, is worth pursuing. The past finally catches up with our hero, though, leaving him with some very difficult decisions to make. Our season finale will change the game forever.

programme.title: Coldplay: Best of the BBC
programme.desc: Coldplay fans will be in Paradise with this trip through the BBC’s archives, which follows the incredible journey that’s taken the band from promising new talents, whose first hits coincided with the start of a new century, right through to stadium-filling global superstars. With all the key songs and anthems taken from a selection of their finest TV performances, this Coldplay mix looks and sounds Magic.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Toby Jones explores an extraordinary acting dynasty on his mum’s side, and he is determined to discover whether his dad’s stories of a connection to India are fact or fiction.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The A to Z of TV Gardening
programme.desc: Carol Kirkwood takes an alphabetical journey through the world of gardening, getting inspiration and advice from some of the BBC's most popular garden presenters and programmes. In this episode, she's exploring subjects that all begin with the letter Q. Programmes include Gardeners' World, The One Show, RHS Chelsea Flower Show and Springwatch, with presenters Monty Don, Chris Packham, Joe Swift, James Alexander Sinclair, Alan Titchmarsh, Nicky Chapman, Andy Sturgeon and Carol Klein.

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Christine Walkden heads for the lakes and fells of Cumbria to visit some more magnificent gardens. At Levens Hall, she lends a hand planting some spring bulbs and hears some of lakeland lad Len's special memories. At Holehird, she meets the dedicated volunteers who have restored this 19th-century garden to its former glory. And we discover the spur to Beatrix Potter's prolific writing career.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Anita continues her east coast road trip, visiting the Naze, a nature reserve on the Essex coast. Here, coastal erosion is particularly severe, with around 2 to 3 metres lost from the cliffs every year. But there are benefits to a crumbling coastline – it can reveal 55 million years of history. Anita joins a group of enthusiastic fossil hunters on the lookout for remnants of the coast's fascinating past. She also discovers what has been done to protect the area’s heritage and visits one of over a thousand brightly coloured beach huts overlooking the North Sea. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the hidden histories found across our landscape.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek revisits three walks that have changed people’s lives. He sees how the great outdoors aided a cancer patient’s recovery and inspired those with sight loss to go birdwatching.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: It's all about the borders at Beechgrove Garden as Brian Cunningham and Kirsty Wilson replant, fill gaps and replace losses all around the plot. Kirsty revisits her hot border, designed to display vibrant colours at the height of summer. The winter temperatures killed off a few plants, so she will be trying out some alternatives. Brian is in the calendar border, created to have some form of colour or interest every month of the year. It has not had much attention this year, so Brian will be topping it up to ensure year-round performance. Kirsty will also be planting in the border behind Beechgrove's main pond, where other gaps have appeared, and she is building a new structure to create a habitat for pollinators. There is a trip to visit a great garden on the Cowal Peninsula, and all the week's handy hints.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt brings the sunshine to the menu with a riot of summertime recipes. Hasan Semay celebrates Turkish mezze with a quartet of outstanding dishes – hummus with chopped salad, atom peppers, deep-fried calamari and bulgur wheat salad. Freddy Bird roasts Iberico pork chops, served with a rich butcher’s sauce, buttery mashed potato and spring greens. Anna Haugh puts Irish cuisine in the spotlight with her balsamic prawns with creamy polenta. And Dr Saliha Mahmood Ahmed has a classic Indian street food snack, aloo bun chaat, and a side of refreshing pani puri. Olly Smith has a whirlwind tour of cheese and wine pairings, and Johannes Radebe tucks into either his food heaven, Thai fried rice with fried chicken, or his food hell, chilled courgette soup. Meanwhile, Rick Stein is on the hunt for the best-tasting carrots, and the Hairy Bikers explore Catalan influences in Italy.

programme.title: Indian Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Food writer and chef Anjum Anand is on a mission to show novice cooks how to cook simple yet delicious Indian food. In this episode she takes a stall at the quintessentially English Sherborne Country Fair where she hopes to persuade the masses to ditch greasy burgers and hot dogs in favour of her healthier alternative, and raise money for charity. She enlists the help of energetic friend Panthea, who is a great sales woman but can't cook, so Anjum decides it is time for her to learn. Anjum shows Panthea how to cook up a tandoori-style feast. There is delicious chicken tikka marinated in ginger, garlic, spices and yoghurt, before being grilled and served in a wrap with crunchy salad. Plus luscious lamb brochettes with a mint and coriander pickle. For the vegetarians, thick tandoori mushrooms with a spinach, peanut and paneer filling. All that is left is for Panthea to master the art of making samosas and the two head off to Dorset to see if they are a match for the burger vans.

programme.title: Indian Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Alex, a friend of Anjum Anand's, is having the boys over to watch the FA Cup Final. His initial thought is an Indian takeaway, but Anjum persuades him to cook up an Indian feast. Having treated him to a tasty breakfast of mango smoothies, they head to the supermarket to pick up ingredients where Alex learns everything there is to know about chillies. Anjum and Alex make spicy lamb burgers made with fresh chillies, ginger, mint and lashings of coriander as well as delicious chilli-chicken - rolled in bread crumbs and oven-baked. Anjum then reveals the ancient art of cheese-making before visiting a top Indian restaurant in London where Head Chef Mehernosh shows her the secrets of kulfi, a rich Indian ice cream.

programme.title: Operation Crossbow
programme.desc: World War II drama. A small group of agents is sent on a vital mission to destroy a Nazi V-2 rocket base in Holland. Their aim is to prevent flying bombs from falling on London.

programme.title: Cricket: The Hundred
programme.desc: Coverage of The Hundred 100-ball cricket tournament.

programme.title: Cricket: The Hundred
programme.desc: Coverage of The Hundred 100-ball cricket tournament.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: This episode of the series is hosted by quick-witted Dara O Briain, who introduces wonderful Australian comic Felicity Ward and the sensational Mo Gilligan to the stage.

programme.title: Taxi Driver
programme.desc: Travis Bickle is an alienated ex-Marine, working nights as a New York cabbie. Haunted by the squalor around him, he is drawn to the beautiful - and 'pure' - Betsy, but his attempts to woo her prove disastrous, and he begins a descent into a personal hell. Cult drama directed by Martin Scorsese and scripted by Paul Schrader.

programme.title: The Elephant Man
programme.desc: In 1884, an ambitious young surgeon is intrigued by a sideshow freak billed as the Elephant Man. He finds, behind the disfigured exhibit, an intelligent person whose rehabilitation he undertakes.

And Dr Saliha Mahmood Ahmed has a classic Indian street food snack, aloo bun chaat, and a side of refreshing pani puri. Olly Smith has a whirlwind tour of cheese and wine pairings, and Johannes Radebe tucks into either his food heaven, Thai fried rice with fried chicken, or his food hell, chilled courgette soup. Meanwhile, Rick Stein is on the hunt for the best-tasting carrots, and the Hairy Bikers explore Catalan influences in Italy.

programme.title: Indian Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Food writer and chef Anjum Anand is on a mission to show novice cooks how to cook simple yet delicious Indian food. In this episode she takes a stall at the quintessentially English Sherborne Country Fair where she hopes to persuade the masses to ditch greasy burgers and hot dogs in favour of her healthier alternative, and raise money for charity. She enlists the help of energetic friend Panthea, who is a great sales woman but can't cook, so Anjum decides it is time for her to learn. Anjum shows Panthea how to cook up a tandoori-style feast. There is delicious chicken tikka marinated in ginger, garlic, spices and yoghurt, before being grilled and served in a wrap with crunchy salad. Plus luscious lamb brochettes with a mint and coriander pickle. For the vegetarians, thick tandoori mushrooms with a spinach, peanut and paneer filling. All that is left is for Panthea to master the art of making samosas and the two head off to Dorset to see if they are a match for the burger vans.

programme.title: Indian Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Alex, a friend of Anjum Anand's, is having the boys over to watch the FA Cup Final. His initial thought is an Indian takeaway, but Anjum persuades him to cook up an Indian feast. Having treated him to a tasty breakfast of mango smoothies, they head to the supermarket to pick up ingredients where Alex learns everything there is to know about chillies. Anjum and Alex make spicy lamb burgers made with fresh chillies, ginger, mint and lashings of coriander as well as delicious chilli-chicken - rolled in bread crumbs and oven-baked. Anjum then reveals the ancient art of cheese-making before visiting a top Indian restaurant in London where Head Chef Mehernosh shows her the secrets of kulfi, a rich Indian ice cream.

programme.desc: Buddy and Conker get a call for help from Jervis in Northern Ireland, a brilliant basketball player who wants a slam-dunk meal for his mum to take to work. She’s always doing things for the family, so he wants to pop something in her lunch box to make her smile! Buddy knows the power of a tasty meal, so he teaches Jervis to make mini quiches that will fit easily in her packed lunch. They make the pastry from scratch, and because they’re homemade, choose whatever fillings Jervis and his mum would like best! Join them as they take time out from the kitchen to shoot some hoops and Buddy learns the essential skills of basketball; controlling the ball, dribbling, defending and shooting. SCOOOORE! Join Buddy, Conker and Jervis as they create super-tasty lunchtime bites in this slam dunk of an episode of Cooking Buddies. You can get all of Buddy’s recipes, and loads more, at bbc.co.uk/food.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. The pressure intensifies as the final looms. A quiz produces unexpected results, leaving Ella desperate to be believed for once, while Billy continues with a high-risk bluff designed to frame Harry and control the narrative. Valuation descends into chaos as accusations fly, emotions boil over and the vote collapses into deadlock. When a rule is broken, the hosts are forced to intervene - triggering a dramatic reversal and a shock exit that reshapes the game. A final quiz redraws the leaderboard before a brutal twist is introduced: players are offered the chance to leave immediately with their winnings. As night falls, the house faces an impossible choice - risk everything or walk away.

programme.title: James Martin's American Adventure
programme.desc: James's American adventure takes the chef to the city of San Francisco this time - he arrives on a boat through the bay before cooking on the SS Jeremiah O'Brien, a great and historic warship. James then takes a walk on foot through San Francisco's famous Chinatown and explores the many food stores offering unusual ingredients to the thousands of shoppers that visit every day - those with a sweet tooth are also catered for in this episode as we get an exclusive look at the Ghiradelli Chocolate Festival, an event which celebrates the sweet stuff in a uniquely Californian way.

programme.title: James Martin's Saturday Morning
programme.desc: James is back in the kitchen on a Saturday morning where he's cooking up a couple of delicious recipes for singer Michael Ball and enjoying dishes from chefs Galton Blackiston, Ruth Hansom and Glynn Purnell.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S]

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Alan is joined at Manor Farm this time by legendary singer Petula Clark - who talks about her illustrious career - Midsomer Murders' Fiona Dolman, who chats about keeping DCI John Barnaby in check, and former NHS doctor-turned-comedian and author Adam Kaye, who talks about the power of laughter. Alan will also be taking a look the ancient art of horseback falconry and celebrating the very best in British chardonnay this time.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton gets up-close-and-personal during the castration of a Bengal cat, and meets Amy the golden retriever and her devoted owner ahead of surgery to remove a lump from her mouth. Later, 12-week-old Labrador retriever puppy Tassie and her new owners are in for a vaccination, and returning canine patients Mono and Marley visit James for their one-year boosters. Pushkins the impatient Persian cat, also a repeat client, is back for help to remove her matted fur. A visiting surgical team is called into The Grove to attend to a bulldog's complex knee injury, and we venture out of the practice to see another specialist at work as clinical animal behaviourist Roz Pooley invites us to experience one of her puppy training classes.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Chef Tom Kerridge is on the road in Tuscany and Lazio, meeting producers who are just as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck, he discovers the traditions behind olive oil and the new techniques that are helping to grow rocket in Lazio. Arriving in stunning Tuscany just as the olive harvest begins, he joins Ricardo to learn how here oil is a matter of honour. Then Tom turns his hand to shaking the olives off the tree and join the taste test of the first press, a tradition handed down through the generations. Tom cooks up a feast to honour the harvest: a fig and extra virgin olive oil cake. His journey then takes him to Lazio, where rocket is an obsession. Giancarlo, a local producer, shows him how they get a peppery intensity into the leaves through careful cultivation. After a hard day's work Tom cooks his take on a family favourite: rocket pesto chicken parmigiana with a pesto pasta salad.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: This time Alan and his team are in Suffolk, where charity shop worker Eileen has a gravel drive and muddy borders as her only garden - with husband Roy suffering from Parkinson's, Eileen is desperate for a peaceful, pretty and safe space for them to share. To create a real garden, Alan designs an inward-looking intimate area surrounded by beautiful year-round colour for Roy and Eileen to enjoy - at the same time, Katie Rushworth is inspired by the couple's love of blues and pinks to plant a wrap-around border and building a covered seating area. Meanwhile, Frances Tophill is tasked with breaking up the vast expanse of fence with clever architectural planting and raised beds, and she must also design a bin store with living roof too - elsewhere, David Domoney heads to Wappenham Manor in Northamptonshire, where the front garden has been transformed into the most spectacular formal garden to welcome the owners home.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world. [S]

programme.title: Live and Let Die
programme.desc: The eighth entry in the James Bond film series and the first to star Roger Moore as 007. James Bond is sent to New York to investigate when three MI6 agents are killed whilst investigating the activities of Dr Kananga - the prime minister of the island of San Monique - and is soon on the trail of a Harlem crime kingpin known as Mr Big. Sensing links between Dr Kananga and Mr Big, Bond follows the men to Louisiana and the Caribbean - and uncovers a horrific plot to flood America with free heroin.

programme.title: The Chase Celebrity Special
programme.desc: Are four celebrities clever enough to take on one of the country's finest quiz brains? Bradley Walsh hosts as Jayde Adams, Tony Cottee, Naughty Boy and The Vivienne take on the challenge in the hope of winning thousands of pounds for their chosen charities.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip. Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Barcelona to take on The Vixen and The Menace, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate across the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the next city - lose and it's the first flight home. Following a competitive opening quiz and a series of city-wide challenges - including hunting for graffiti art, tackling a theme park drop ride, and playing a football shirt game - the competition remains unpredictable and the race is tight with a dramatic finale.

programme.title: ITV Evening News
programme.desc: National and international news with reports and analysis from ITV's Correspondents in the UK and around the world as well as the latest major sports results. [S]

programme.title: ITV News Anglia
programme.desc: The latest news and weather from the East of England. [S]

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As climate change accelerates, weather across the planet is becoming more extreme, more violent, and less predictable - a burrowing owl mother on the American prairies must use her extraordinary hearing and a network of underground burrows to save her scattered chicks from intensifying tornadoes, two veteran cheetah brothers in Kenya face record-breaking floods that force them to swim raging rivers and confront deadly rivals before one hunting alone uses the storms to his advantage, a young polar bear in the Arctic loses the summer sea ice she depends on and is driven to stalk reindeer on land, and a troop of chimpanzees in drought-stricken Senegal dig wells and descend into abandoned gold mines in a desperate search for water. These animals across a warming world reveal resilience, ingenuity and courage, but adaptation has limits in the face of relentless change.

Desperate, Monica uses a press conference to provoke the killer. Nichol tells Barclay about Bethany's affair and he attacks Stephen, leading to his arrest. Monica gets information which points to James being the killer and they arrest him. Monica goes home, but wakes to discover that the killer has murdered Philly.

programme.title: Terror in the Skies: Stopping the Liquid Bomb Plot
programme.desc: Gripping documentary revealing the untold story of the 2006 liquid bomb plot and the frantic race to stop it. Discover the huge covert operation swung into action to stop this tero

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Rylan faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Has he ever considered a real suntan? Is honesty always the best policy? From cancelled celebrity friends to the contents of his bedside table, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Rylan opens up about infidelity, heartbreak, estrangement from his father and the breakdown that forced him to take life day by day. He reflects on fame, loneliness and coming out, while also helping Natalie figure out how to get her girlfriend down the aisle and revealing whether he and his mum compare notes on guys. Along the way there are huge laughs, unexpected tangents and moments of real vulnerability as The Assembly push Rylan further than he's ever been pushed before. The episode ends with a powerful performance of his favourite song. Expect chaos, honesty, emotion and a side of Rylan rarely seen on television.

programme.desc: James's American adventure takes the chef to the city of San Francisco this time - he arrives on a boat through the bay before cooking on the SS Jeremiah O'Brien, a great and historic warship. programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: Alan is joined at Manor Farm this time by legendary singer Petula Clark - who talks about her illustrious career - Midsomer Murders' Fiona Dolman, who chats about keeping DCI John Barnaby in check, and former NHS doctor-turned-comedian and author Adam Kaye, who talks about the power of laughter. Alan will also be taking a look the ancient art of horseback falconry and celebrating the very best in British chardonnay this time.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton gets up-close-and-personal during the castration of a Bengal cat, and meets Amy the golden retriever and her devoted owner ahead of surgery to remove a lump from her mouth. Later, 12-week-old Labrador retriever puppy Tassie and her new owners are in for a vaccination, and returning canine patients Mono and Marley visit James for their one-year boosters. Pushkins the impatient Persian cat, also a repeat client, is back for help to remove her matted fur. A visiting surgical team is called into The Grove to attend to a bulldog's complex knee injury, and we venture out of the practice to see another specialist at work as clinical animal behaviourist Roz Pooley invites us to experience one of her puppy training classes.

programme.title: Tom Kerridge Cooks...
programme.desc: Chef Tom Kerridge is on the road in Tuscany and Lazio, meeting producers who are just as obsessed with growing ingredients as he is about cooking them. In his bespoke, vintage food truck, he discovers the traditions behind olive oil and the new techniques that are helping to grow rocket in Lazio. Arriving in stunning Tuscany just as the olive harvest begins, he joins Ricardo to learn how here oil is a matter of honour. Then Tom turns his hand to shaking the olives off the tree and join the taste test of the first press, a tradition handed down through the generations. Tom cooks up a feast to honour the harvest: a fig and extra virgin olive oil cake. His journey then takes him to Lazio, where rocket is an obsession. Giancarlo, a local producer, shows him how they get a peppery intensity into the leaves through careful cultivation. After a hard day's work Tom cooks his take on a family favourite: rocket pesto chicken parmigiana with a pesto pasta salad.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: This time Alan and his team are in Suffolk, where charity shop worker Eileen has a gravel drive and muddy borders as her only garden - with husband Roy suffering from Parkinson's, Eileen is desperate for a peaceful, pretty and safe space for them to share. To create a real garden, Alan designs an inward-looking intimate area surrounded by beautiful year-round colour for Roy and Eileen to enjoy - at the same time, Katie Rushworth is inspired by the couple's love of blues and pinks to plant a wrap-around border and building a covered seating area. Meanwhile, Frances Tophill is tasked with breaking up the vast expanse of fence with clever architectural planting and raised beds, and she must also design a bin store with living roof too - elsewhere, David Domoney heads to Wappenham Manor in Northamptonshire, where the front garden has been transformed into the most spectacular formal garden to welcome the owners home.

programme.title: Live and Let Die
programme.desc: The eighth entry in the James Bond film series and the first to star Roger Moore as 007. Sensing links between Dr Kananga and Mr Big, Bond follows the men to Louisiana and the Caribbean - and uncovers a horrific plot to flood America with free heroin.

In his bespoke, vintage food truck, he discovers the traditions behind olive oil and the new techniques that are helping to grow rocket in Lazio. Arriving in stunning Tuscany just as the olive harvest begins, he joins Ricardo to learn how here oil is a matter of honour. Then Tom turns his hand to shaking the olives off the tree and join the taste test of the first press, a tradition handed down through the generations. Tom cooks up a feast to honour the harvest: a fig and extra virgin olive oil cake. His journey then takes him to Lazio, where rocket is an obsession. Giancarlo, a local producer, shows him how they get a peppery intensity into the leaves through careful cultivation. After a hard day's work Tom cooks his take on a family favourite: rocket pesto chicken parmigiana with a pesto pasta salad.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: This time Alan and his team are in Suffolk, where charity shop worker Eileen has a gravel drive and muddy borders as her only garden - with husband Roy suffering from Parkinson's, Eileen is desperate for a peaceful, pretty and safe space for them to share. To create a real garden, Alan designs an inward-looking intimate area surrounded by beautiful year-round colour for Roy and Eileen to enjoy - at the same time, Katie Rushworth is inspired by the couple's love of blues and pinks to plant a wrap-around border and building a covered seating area. Meanwhile, Frances Tophill is tasked with breaking up the vast expanse of fence with clever architectural planting and raised beds, and she must also design a bin store with living roof too - elsewhere, David Domoney heads to Wappenham Manor in Northamptonshire, where the front garden has been transformed into the most spectacular formal garden to welcome the owners home.

programme.title: The Chase Around The World
programme.desc: The Chase Around The World is a six-part series where Bradley and The Chasers escape the studio to challenge contestants on the world's smartest road trip. Six pairs set off on an epic chase around some of the world's most incredible cities, aiming to win the £100,000 prize. The teams land in Barcelona to take on The Vixen and The Menace, who have set a series of quiz questions that the teams must solve to navigate across the city and find Bradley at the finish line. Competition is fierce as teams do not want to finish last, if they do they face a head-to-head showdown with the Chasers. The final pair will need to beat them to join the other teams and head onto the next city - lose and it's the first flight home. Following a competitive opening quiz and a series of city-wide challenges - including hunting for graffiti art, tackling a theme park drop ride, and playing a football shirt game - the competition remains unpredictable and the race is tight with a dramatic finale.

programme.title: Force Of Nature
programme.desc: Documentary series revealing the incredible ways in which all life is impacted by our journey around the Sun. As climate change accelerates, weather across the planet is becoming more extreme, more violent, and less predictable - a burrowing owl mother on the American prairies must use her extraordinary hearing and a network of underground burrows to save her scattered chicks from intensifying tornadoes, two veteran cheetah brothers in Kenya face record-breaking floods that force them to swim raging rivers and confront deadly rivals before one hunting alone uses the storms to his advantage, a young polar bear in the Arctic loses the summer sea ice she depends on and is driven to stalk reindeer on land, and a troop of chimpanzees in drought-stricken Senegal dig wells and descend into abandoned gold mines in a desperate search for water. These animals across a warming world reveal resilience, ingenuity and courage, but adaptation has limits in the face of relentless change.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Rylan faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Has he ever considered a real suntan? Is honesty always the best policy? From cancelled celebrity friends to the contents of his bedside table, nothing is off limits. As the questions come thick and fast, Rylan opens up about infidelity, heartbreak, estrangement from his father and the breakdown that forced him to take life day by day. He reflects on fame, loneliness and coming out, while also helping Natalie figure out how to get her girlfriend down the aisle and revealing whether he and his mum compare notes on guys. Along the way there are huge laughs, unexpected tangents and moments of real vulnerability as The Assembly push Rylan further than he's ever been pushed before. The episode ends with a powerful performance of his favourite song. Expect chaos, honesty, emotion and a side of Rylan rarely seen on television.

programme.title: Fern Britton: Inside the Vet's
programme.desc: Fern Britton gets up-close-and-personal during the castration of a Bengal cat, and meets Amy the golden retriever and her devoted owner ahead of surgery to remove a lump from her mouth. Later, 12-week-old Labrador retriever puppy Tassie and her new owners are in for a vaccination, and returning canine patients Mono and Marley visit James for their one-year boosters.
